items.title: Pay amount demanded in Mahnbescheid
items.quote: Der Betrag ist bis zum 15.01.2027 zu zahlen.
items.computation: The letter prints an explicit calendar date rather than a period to count: 'bis zum 15.01.2027'. Used as stated. Note: this is only seven calendar days after the stated issue date (08.01.2027), which is unusually short and inconsistent with how a genuine German court Mahnbescheid works — a real Mahnbescheid does not set a short payment deadline like an invoice; instead it must grant the recipient a two-week period to file a Widerspruch (objection) under § 692 ZPO, with that right clearly stated. This letter contains no Widerspruch/Rechtsbehelfsbelehrung at all, so the legitimacy of this '15.01.2027' payment demand itself is doubtful.

warnings: This letter has strong hallmarks of a scam impersonating a German court: the sender 'Mahngericht Beispielstadt', the recipient 'Anton Musterschmidt', and the creditor 'Beispiel Online-Spielothek Ltd.' all use generic placeholder-style German names ('Beispielstadt' = 'example city', 'Musterschmidt' = 'sample-smith') rather than a real institution and person.

No court named 'Mahngericht Beispielstadt' exists in Germany; genuine centralised dunning courts have specific names (e.g. Amtsgericht Hagen, Berlin-Wedding, Coburg, Stuttgart). Verify the actual issuing court independently before taking any action.

By law a genuine Mahnbescheid must contain a Rechtsbehelfsbelehrung informing the recipient of the right to file a Widerspruch (objection) within two weeks of service (§ 692 ZPO). This letter contains no such instruction whatsoever, which is a serious red flag for a fake court document.

The letter demands payment exclusively into a private law-firm account ('Kanzlei Brandner Forderungsservice', IBAN DE10 7005 0000 0044 7120 91) rather than to the court or clearly to the named creditor, combined with urgent pressure and threats of immediate enforcement (Vollstreckungsbescheid, Gerichtsvollzieher) — a known pattern used in fake debt-collection/court scams. Do not transfer any money before independently verifying this claim with an official source (e.g. by looking up the real court's contact details yourself, not those printed on this letter).

The very short 7-day gap between the stated issue date (08.01.2027) and the payment deadline (15.01.2027) is inconsistent with standard German Mahnverfahren procedure and supports the suspicion that this is not a genuine court letter.
